mode: VERIFICATION (Thompson 1917 claim override) — not a new-model scout

claim.source: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. IX 'On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons', pp. 411-487, Figs. 194-235
claim.text: Sponge and alcyonarian spicule forms (needles, tri-/tetraradiates and their aggregates) are the forms physical deposition/crystallisation takes within the cell/field that secretes them.
operational_form_tested: P1 (p. 445, Fig. 214 F): a skeletal deposit laid down between / within the partitions of three contiguous cells takes a triradiate form whose ray axes meet at equal angles of 120 deg (Plateau junction).

P2 (pp. 445-446, Fig. 214 A, C): the equiangular condition is modified by any inequality in the specific tensions of adjacent cells; the surface (sagittal) case gives a spicule with TWO EQUAL angles and ONE UNEQUAL angle, in the limit two rays 'nearly in a straight line, and at right angles to the third' (p. 443).
P3 (p. 446, Fig. 214 E): four cells in solid contact give a four-rayed spicule with rays at the tetrahedral angle of about 109 deg.
P4 (p. 446): rays of a spicule formed in the interspace of three contiguous equal circles have concave sides (curvilinear equilateral triangle / Plateau bourrelet).
claim.mechanism_family: geometric-mechanistic (surface-tension / Plateau-border force balance, Neumann triangle)

dataset.title: Data from: Three-dimensionally preserved soft-tissues and calcareous hexactins in a Silurian sponge: implications for early sponge evolution.
dataset.authors: Nadhira A, Sutton M, Botting J, Muir L, Gueriau P, King A, Briggs D, Siveter D, Siveter D
dataset.primary_article: Nadhira et al. (2019) Royal Society Open Science 6:190911, doi:10.1098/rsos.190911 (Crossref-verified 2026-10-28)

mismatch_reasons: Taxon/material: Carduispongia pedicula is a Silurian fossil reticulosan with calcareous HEXACTINE (six-rayed, orthogonal) spicules in a single orthogonal layer. Thompson's quantitative predictions (P1-P3) concern the TRIRADIATE and TETRAXON spicules of living calcareous sponges (Grantia and allies) formed between 3 or 4 contiguous cells; Thompson himself calls the hexactinellid case 'somewhat harder to understand' (p. 443) and offers no 3-cell/4-cell angle prediction for it.

Variables: the dataset is 5.8 GB of tomogram slices (BMP) and VAXML/STL surface reconstructions of whole specimens; it contains no spicule ray-angle table, and extracting single-spicule ray axes from a whole-body synchrotron mesh of a compressed fossil is outside what this loop can validate.
Size: 5.83 GB cannot be vendored or SHA-256-pinned in this repository; only the Dryad API metadata and per-file Dryad MD5 digests are pinned.
preassigned_dataset_verification.qualitative_use_only: The 90 deg orthogonal hexactine network of C. pedicula is cited as the n=6 (cubic) limiting case alongside Thompson's 3-cell (120 deg) and 4-cell (109.47 deg) predictions, with no verdict weight.

fig_214_page.content: Fig. 214. Spicules of Grantia and other calcareous sponges (after Haeckel): A, B T-shaped sagittal triradiates; C sagittal with curved outer rays; D sagittal; E tetractine; F regular equiangular triradiate.
fig_214_page.license: public domain (1917; author d. 1948; US pre-1929)

sanctioned_alternative_dataset.status: Haeckel's drawings as reproduced by Thompson are the author's own evidence base: same taxon (Grantia / Calcarea), same variables (ray angles, sagittal symmetry). Treated as the SOURCE-FIGURE dataset; drawings, not photographs, so used as the secondary sample.

literature_hits_openalex.title: Crystallographic orientation and concentric layers in spicules of calcareous sponges
literature_hits_openalex.relevance: Modern confirmation that each calcareous spicule is a single calcite crystal whose c-axis is NOT aligned with the ray axes (Thompson p. 444: 'its axes are not crystalline axes ... a crystal under restraint').

literature_hits_openalex.title: Spicule formation in calcareous sponges: Coordinated expression of biomineralization genes and spicule-type specific genes
literature_hits_openalex.relevance: Modern cell biology: triactines are formed by a sextet of six sclerocytes (three founder + three thickener cells), tetractines by a septet; the deposition field is the cell group, as Thompson argued, though the cells are specialised sclerocytes, not arbitrary neighbours.

literature_hits_openalex.title: Spicule formation in the calcareous sponge Sycon ciliatum
literature_hits_openalex.relevance: Ledger & Jones: founder/thickener sclerocyte pairs per ray; the mechanistic counterpoint to Thompson's 'between any three cells' picture.

literature_hits_openalex.title: Three-dimensionally preserved soft tissues and calcareous hexactins in a Silurian sponge
literature_hits_openalex.relevance: Primary article of the pre-assigned Dryad dataset (hexactine, orthogonal case).

verdict_plan: Measure ray angles on segmented triactines/tetractines; test P1 (equiangular mode near 120 deg in the light-microscope population), P2 (paired-angle equality |a2-a3| << |a1-a2| vs a Dirichlet random-partition null; one-parameter Neumann family cos(theta_pair) = -rho/2), P3 (tetrahedral angle of the tetractine apical ray in projection is not testable from a 2D plate: reported as UNTESTABLE here).
